**(a) Data.** A **dust model** on $U$ is a pair $(\rho,u)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\rho:U\to\mathbb R$ with $\rho(p)>0$ for every $p\in U$,
  the **rest density**; and
- a smooth future-directed unit timelike vector field $u$ on $U$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]] with target $TM$
  described through the tangent bundle; concretely, $u$ is a smooth vector
  field on $U$ with $g_p(u_p,u_p)=-1$ and $g_p(u_p,N_p)<0$ at every $p$,
  [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

The parameter $\rho$ is the coefficient in the unit-normalized tensor of
clause (b); this mathematical definition assigns it no physical unit. In the
framework's SI stress-energy reading it is the **rest energy density**
$\varepsilon:=\rho$, in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$. The **rest-mass
density** is instead $\rho_m:=\varepsilon/c^2$, in
$\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, and the physical four-velocity is
$U:=cu$, with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. Thus the same tensor is
$T^{ab}=\varepsilon u^au^b=\rho_m U^aU^b$. A purely mathematical or
$c=1$ convention may rescale the density coefficient; interpreting $\rho$
as an SI mass density while keeping the unit tangent $u$ would require the
explicit tensor $c^2\rho\,u\otimes u$. Physical realizations and readings
are adopted by the matter postulate, not deduced here.

**(b) Stress-energy tensor.** The model's **stress-energy tensor** has the
smooth symmetric contravariant components and their covariant lowering

$$T^{ab}:=\rho\,u^au^b\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad T_{ab}=\rho\,u_au_b,$$

with $u_a=g_{ac}u^c$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]); the two expressions correspond
under raising both indices, by $g^{ac}g^{bd}T_{cd}=T^{ab}$.

**(c) Dust system.** The **dust system** on $U$ is the pair of equations

$$\nabla_a(\rho\,u^a)=0,\qquad u^a\nabla_au^b=0 .$$

The first is a continuity equation for the density current $\rho u$; the
second says that the integral curves of $u$ are geodesics in the parameter that
makes $u$ their unit tangent, i.e. that the dust particles are in free fall
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
matter domain ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Dust.** Let $(\rho,u)$ be a dust model on $U$, and let
$T_{ab}:=\rho u_a u_b$ be its derived tensor
([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]). Then

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0\ \text{on }U\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad \nabla_a(\rho u^a)=0\ \text{and}\ u^a\nabla_au^b=0\ \text{on }U .$$

**(b) Perfect fluid.** Let $(\varepsilon,p,n)$ be a perfect-fluid model on
$U$, with derived tensor $T_{ab}:=(\varepsilon+p)n_an_b+p g_{ab}$,
comoving derivative $D$, expansion $\vartheta$, acceleration $a$ and
projection $h$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Then

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0\ \text{on }U\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+p)\vartheta=0\quad\text{and}\quad (\varepsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0\ \text{on }U .$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
subset carrying the restricted smooth structure of
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]],
choose an orientation on $U$ and its metric volume form (independent of the
time orientation), let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) — in an application this is the
stress-energy tensor field of the model's matter sector
([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]) — and let $\xi$ be a Killing field of
$(M,g)$ on $U$ ([[def-gr-killing-field]],
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]] clause (a)) that is
everywhere timelike and future-directed,

$$g_p(\xi_p,\xi_p)<0,\qquad g_p(\xi_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in U .$$

Put $X:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ on $U$ and $n:=\xi/X$, an observer congruence on
$U$: $g(n,n)=-1$ and $g(n,N)=g(\xi,N)/X<0$
([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]).

**(a) Killing current.** The **Killing current** of the pair $(T,\xi)$ is the
smooth vector field on $U$

$$J_\xi{}^a:=T^{ab}\xi_b .$$

Since $\xi=Xn$ and $J^a=-T^{ab}n_b$, one has
$T^{ab}\xi_b=-XJ^a$, where $J=-T(\cdot,n)$ is the measured
energy-momentum current of [[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]]; no
conservation of $J_\xi$ is asserted by this definition.

**(b) Killing charge of a three-chain.** For every finite smooth singular
$3$-chain $\Sigma$ of $M$ contained in $U$, the **Killing charge** of $\Sigma$
with respect to $\xi$ is the real number

$$Q_\xi(\Sigma):=-\Phi_{J_\xi}(\Sigma),$$

where $\Phi_{J_\xi}$ is the flux of the current $J_\xi$ through
$3$-chains on the oriented open submanifold $U$ in the sense of [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]
clause (b).

When $\xi$ is normalized with a length-valued flow parameter in the SI
length-coordinate convention, this charge is read as a **Killing energy**.

**(c) Relation to the measured energy current.** Since $J_\xi=-XJ$,

$$Q_\xi(\Sigma)=\Phi_{XJ}(\Sigma),$$

the flux of the redshift-weighted measured energy current $XJ$. For a
$3$-simplex $\sigma$ that is non-null with velocity basis $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ and
adapted unit normal $\nu^{*}$ (so that $(\nu^{*},v_1,v_2,v_3)$ is positively
oriented and $\varepsilon:=g(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})\in\{-1,1\}$), the pullback of
$\iota_{XJ}\mathrm{vol}_g$ is
$\varepsilon\,g(XJ,\nu^{*})\sqrt{|\det(g(v_i,v_j))|}\,dt^1\wedge dt^2\wedge dt^3$
([[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] clause (c)); when
$\nu^{*}=-n$ and the $v_i$ span $n^{\perp}$ this coefficient equals
$-X\mu\sqrt{|\det(g(v_i,v_j))|}$, so up to the orientation sign carried by the
adapted normal, $Q_\xi(\Sigma)$ is the integral of the redshift-weighted
measured energy density $X\mu$ over $\Sigma$. The factor $X$ carries the
normalization and units of $\xi$.

**(d) Reading and scope.** $Q_\xi(\Sigma)$ is the charge that the model
assigns to the chain $\Sigma$ under the symmetry $\xi$, in the framework
of the postulates [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]],
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]] with the assigned tensor and symmetry; it does not require the field law
for its definition. Under the unit conventions of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]], if $T$ is read in
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and the flow parameter of $\xi$ is measured in
metres, then $X$ is dimensionless and $Q_\xi(\Sigma)$ is read in $\mathrm J$.
More generally, if that parameter has unit $\mathcal S$, then in a
length-coordinate chart $X$ has units $\mathrm m/\mathcal S$ and $Q_\xi$ has
units $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m/\mathcal S$; converting it to an energy requires
an explicitly specified normalization factor. The value depends on the model,
on $\xi$ (replacing $\xi$ by a dimensionless constant multiple $\lambda\xi$
with $\lambda>0$ multiplies $X$, $J_\xi$ and $Q_\xi$ by $\lambda$), and on the
chain $\Sigma$. The definition asserts no conservation, no positivity, no
finiteness for unbounded chains and no measured value. If additionally
$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$, the Killing
current lemma gives conservation up to the side flux. The field law
([[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] or [[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]])
is one way to supply this divergence condition; it is not necessary for
the mathematical conservation implication. If no
timelike Killing field exists on $U$, $Q_\xi$ is not defined by this item.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
subset carrying the restricted smooth structure of
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]],
let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), and let $n$ be a smooth observer
congruence on $U$ ([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]), so that
$g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $n_p$ is future-directed at every $p\in U$.

**(a) Spatial projection field.** Let

$$h^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$$

on $U$, the component expression of the field of $g$-orthogonal projections
onto the rest spaces $n_p^{\perp}$ of [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]
([[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]); at every $p$ one has
$h^a{}_bn^b=0$, $n_a h^a{}_b=0$, $h^a{}_bh^b{}_c=h^a{}_c$ and
$h^a{}_a=3$. The field is smooth because $n$, $g$ and the identity are smooth
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]).

**(b) Measured energy density.** The **measured energy density** of $T$ for the
congruence $n$ is the smooth function

$$\mu:=T_{ab}n^an^b:U\to\mathbb R .$$

**(c) Energy-momentum current.** The **energy-momentum current** of $T$ for the
congruence $n$ is the smooth vector field on $U$ obtained by raising one index
of $T$ with the inverse metric and contracting with $n$,

$$J^a:=-T^{ab}n_b,$$

with $T^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}T_{cd}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]); the minus sign is the convention that
fixes the energy-component sign convention. A positive $\mu$
alone does not imply that $J$ is causal: $J$ may have an arbitrarily large
spatial part. No future-causal property of $J$ is imposed by this definition.

**(d) Energy flux.** The **energy flux** of $T$ for the congruence $n$ is the
smooth vector field

$$\Phi^a:=h^a{}_bJ^b=J^a-\mu n^a,$$

the spatial projection of $J$; it satisfies $n_a\Phi^a=0$ and
$\Phi^a=-h^a{}_bT^{bc}n_c$.

**(e) Spatial stress.** The **spatial stress** of $T$ for the congruence $n$ is
the smooth field obtained by projecting both tensor slots,

$$S^{ab}:=h^a{}_ch^b{}_dT^{cd},$$

which is symmetric in $a,b$ and satisfies $S^{ab}n_b=0$.

The identities $\mu=-J^an_a$, $J=\mu n+\Phi$, $S^{ab}n_b=0$ and the orthogonal
decomposition

$$T^{ab}=\mu n^an^b+n^a\Phi^b+n^b\Phi^a+S^{ab},$$

together with the uniqueness of that decomposition and the component formulas
in a $g$-orthonormal frame, are proved in
[[lem-gr-observer-energy-momentum-decomposition]]; this definition asserts
none of them. The physical reading and the units of $\mu$, $\Phi$ and $S$ are
fixed by the framework's reading on this page and are not asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$, let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
subset, and let $\xi$ be a smooth Killing field on $U$
([[def-gr-killing-field]]) that is everywhere timelike and future-directed,

$$g_p(\xi_p,\xi_p)<0,\qquad g_p(\xi_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in U .$$

Put $X:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}:U\to(0,\infty)$ (the positive square root) and
$n:=\xi/X$, so that $n$ is a smooth observer congruence on $U$. Let $T$ be a
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$ with
$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$, let $\mu$, $J$, $\Phi$, $S$ be the fields of
[[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]], and let $a$, $\theta$, $D$ be the
kinematic fields of [[def-gr-congruence-acceleration-and-expansion]]. Then:

**(a) Normalization is constant along the congruence, and the acceleration is
a spatial gradient.**

$$n^a\nabla_aX=0,\qquad a_a=\nabla_a\ln X=\frac{1}{X}\nabla_aX,$$

equivalently $\nabla_aX=Xa_a$ and $a=\nabla\ln X$ is the spatial gradient of
$\ln X$.

**(b) Vanishing expansion and symmetric part.** $\theta=0$ and

$$\nabla_an_b+\nabla_bn_a=-(n_aa_b+n_ba_a).$$

**(c) The divergence source is the acceleration term.**
$T^{ab}\nabla_an_b=J^aa_a=\Phi^aa_a$, and consequently

$$\nabla_aJ^a=-\Phi^aa_a .$$

**(d) Conservation of the redshift-weighted current.** On $U$,

$$\nabla_a(XJ^a)=0,\qquad \nabla_a\bigl(T^{ab}\xi_b\bigr)=0 .$$

For the following flux assertion choose an orientation on $U$ and the
volume form of the restricted metric. Then for every finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C$ of $M$ contained in
$U$ with induced boundary $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$,

$$\Phi_{XJ}(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_{XJ}(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_{XJ}(B),$$

where $\Phi_{XJ}$ is the flux of the smooth vector field $XJ$
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b)).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with an
orientation, metric-selected connection $\nabla$, metric volume form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ and current flux $\Phi_J$ as in
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]], and let $J$ be a smooth vector
field on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Write
$\nabla_aJ^a$ for the divergence of $J$.

**(a) Exterior derivative of the current form.** As smooth $4$-forms on $M$,

$$d\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)=\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

**(b) Flux balance (Stokes).** For every finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C$
of $M$ — a finite formal real sum of smooth singular $4$-simplices, the
library convention `def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes` restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — and the flux
$\Phi_J$ of the induced boundary $3$-chain
([[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]],
[[thm-stokes-theorem-for-smooth-singular-chains]]),

$$\Phi_J(\partial C)=\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

Consequently, if $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$ for smooth singular $3$-chains
$\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,B$, then

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)+\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

In particular, if $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ on $C$ then
$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)$, and if moreover
$\Phi_J(B)=0$ then $\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)=\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)$: equal charges need a
vanishing side flux, not merely a divergence-free current.

**(c) Non-null face formula.** Let $\sigma$ be a smooth singular $3$-simplex —
a map $\sigma:\Delta^3\to M$ admitting a smooth extension to a neighbourhood
of the standard $3$-simplex inside its affine plane, the convention restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — that is
non-null at a parameter point $t$
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (c)), with
$v_i:=\sigma_*\partial_i|_t$ spanning the hyperplane $H$ and with the unit
normal $\nu^{*}$ adapted to the ordered basis $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ as in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (c); write
$\varepsilon:=g_{\sigma(t)}(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})\in\{-1,1\}$. Then

$$\sigma^{*}\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)(\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)\big|_{t} =\varepsilon\,g_{\sigma(t)}\bigl(J,\nu^{*}\bigr)\sqrt{\bigl|\det\bigl(g_{\sigma(t)}(v_i,v_j)\bigr)\bigr|} .$$

Equivalently, the tangent vector $J$ is decomposed as
$J=\varepsilon g(J,\nu^{*})\nu^{*}+w'$ with $w'\in H$, and only the normal
component contributes to the flux through the face.

derivations.claim: (Hypotheses.) By [L2], $\xi$ is a Killing field that is everywhere timelike and future-directed, with $X=1$ and $n=\xi$; by [L3] the constant dust $(\rho,\partial_0)$ satisfies the dust system and $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$. Hence the Killing-current construction applies and the conservation and symmetry hypotheses of [L5] are met; no gravitational field equation is used.

(The Killing current and its three-form.) By [L1], $\xi_b=\eta_{b0}=-\delta^0{}_b$, so $J_\xi{}^a=T^{ab}\xi_b=\rho\,u^au^b\xi_b=\rho\,\partial_0^a(u^0\xi_0)=\rho\,\partial_0^a(1\cdot(-1))=-\rho\,\partial_0^a$. Since $\iota_{\partial_0}\mathrm{vol}_g=dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$ by [L1], linearity of the interior product gives $\iota_{J_\xi}\mathrm{vol}_g=-\rho\,dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. This proves clause 2.

(Killing energy on slice chains.) Let $\sigma$ be a smooth singular $3$-simplex of $M$ whose chart velocity vectors at every parameter point are $\sigma_*\partial_i=\partial_i$ for $i=1,2,3$ (so that its image lies in a constant-$x^0$ slice and it is parametrized by the slice coordinates). Then $\sigma^*(dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3)=dt^1\wedge dt^2\wedge dt^3$, so by the definition of the flux through a simplex as the integral of the pulled-back current form, $\Phi_{J_\xi}(\sigma)=-\rho\int_{\Delta^3}dt^1\wedge dt^2\wedge dt^3$. By additivity of the flux over finite chains the same formula holds for every finite smooth singular $3$-chain $\Sigma$ with the stated velocity vectors, and $Q_\xi(\Sigma)=-\Phi_{J_\xi}(\Sigma)=\rho\int_\Sigma dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$ by [L4]. This proves clause 3.

(Conservation and side flux.) By [L5] applied to the present Killing field, $Q_\xi(\Sigma_2)-Q_\xi(\Sigma_1)=-Q_\xi(B)$ for every finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C$ with $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$. If the velocity vectors of every simplex of $B$ span a hyperplane containing $\partial_0$, then the four arguments $J_\xi,v_1,v_2,v_3$ of $\mathrm{vol}_g$ are linearly dependent — $J_\xi$ is a constant multiple of $\partial_0$ — so $\iota_{J_\xi}\mathrm{vol}_g$ vanishes on them and $\Phi_{J_\xi}(B)=0$, whence $Q_\xi(B)=0$ and $Q_\xi(\Sigma_2)=Q_\xi(\Sigma_1)$. This proves clause 4 and completes the verification.

boundaries.reason: The example's model is the constant dust on all of $\mathbb R^4$; no vacuum region, empty slice or empty chain is among its instances.

boundaries.evidence: step 3.1: for slice chains the flux is $\rho\int_\Sigma dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and step 4.1 disposes of the vanishing side-flux case when the side hyperplane contains $\partial_0$.

steps 1.1 and 2.1: the normalisation is $X=1$ because $g(\xi,\xi)=-1$; with $x^0=ct$ this is the length-normalized time-translation field, and the current reduces to $-\rho\,\partial_0$. Thus this example's charge has joule units.

boundaries.reason: $\xi=\partial_0$ is unit timelike everywhere, so the null or vanishing-normalisation case cannot arise, and the dust congruence is nondegenerate.

boundaries.evidence: step 4.1: the endpoint chains $\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2$ enter only through the boundary decomposition, and equality of the charges is asserted precisely when the side term $Q_\xi(B)$ vanishes.

boundaries.reason: The model, the Killing field and the chains are displayed explicitly; the verification selects nothing, and $X=1$ is forced rather than chosen.
The example asserts no equivalence; conservation across slices is instantiated from the theorem's one-way statement carrying its side-flux hypothesis.
No converse is claimed; the example does not assert that equality of the Killing energies forces the side flux to vanish.

risk_review.notes: Read steps 1.1–4.1 with dust, Killing and form suppliers. Constant dust and partial0 are conserved on flat space; Jxi=-rho partial0 gives minus rho dx1 wedge dx2 wedge dx3, and the charge minus sign restores positive coordinate-volume reading. For the stipulated slice parametrizations pullback is dt1 wedge dt2 wedge dt3; finite-chain linearity handles signed/zero chains. Alternating volume vanishes on sides tangent to partial0 without a non-null hypothesis. X=1 and length coordinate x0=ct justify joules; prescribed nonzero dust is explicitly not asserted to solve the flat Einstein equation, and no measured energy is claimed.

citations.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty
open subset, carrying the restricted smooth structure of
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]].

**(a) Congruences.** An **observer congruence** on $U$ is a smooth vector field
$n$ on $U$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]) such that
$n_q$ is an observer at $q$ for every $q\in U$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]); explicitly,

$$g_q(n_q,n_q)=-1\quad\text{and}\quad g_q(n_q,N_q)<0\qquad\text{for every }q\in U .$$

Since $g_q(n_q,n_q)=-1$, the field $n$ is nowhere vanishing. A single observer
at a point is therefore not a congruence, and a congruence is not an ordered
basis or frame of $T_qM$.

**(b) Observer curves.** Because $n$ is a smooth vector field on $U$, the
theorem on maximal integral curves
([[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]],
[[def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field]]) assigns to every $q\in U$ a unique
maximal integral curve $\gamma_q:I_q\to U$ of $n$ with $\gamma_q(0)=q$,
defined on an open interval $I_q\subseteq\mathbb R$. We call these curves the
**observers** (or **observer curves**) of the congruence. Each curve is regular:
for every $s\in I_q$, $\gamma_q'(s)=n_{\gamma_q(s)}$ and

$$g_{\gamma_q(s)}\bigl(n_{\gamma_q(s)},n_{\gamma_q(s)}\bigr)=-1,$$

so its tangent is nonzero, unit timelike and future-directed. Completeness of
the maximal intervals $I_q$, and global product or foliation structure of
$U$, are not asserted. The parameter $s$ is the flow parameter of $n$; it is
not identified with any clock reading here.

**(c) Adapted charts.** An **$n$-adapted chart** is a smooth chart
$(u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3):U'\to\mathbb R^4$ of $M$ whose domain $U'$ is a nonempty
open subset of $U$ and whose **spatial coordinates** $u^1,u^2,u^3$ are constant
along every integral curve $\gamma:J\to U'$ of the restricted field
$n|_{U'}$, where $J$ is an interval. Equivalently, for each maximal observer
curve $\gamma_q:I_q\to U$, each connected component $K$ of
$\gamma_q^{-1}(U')$ (a maximal nonempty interval contained in this open
subset of $\mathbb R$), and $i=1,2,3$, the function
$u^i\circ\gamma_q$ is constant on $K$. If $q\in U'$ and $0\in K$, this
constant is $u^i(q)$. This condition does not identify labels on different
components when a maximal curve leaves and re-enters $U'$. No global adapted
chart, and no adapted chart on all of $U$, is
asserted by this definition; one exists near every point of $U$ by the
existence corollary proved on this page.

**(d) Scope.** A congruence is a field of observer directions on an open set; it
is not a chart, not a tetrad field, and not a family of parametrized
worldlines with specified domains. The physical reading of its observer curves
as ideal-clock worldlines, and the identification of the flow parameter with a
measurable time, belong to the physical postulates of the framework and are not
asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(a) Observers.** An **observer at $p$** is a tangent vector
$n\in T_pM$ such that $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ is future-directed in the sense of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], that is, $g_p(n,N_p)<0$. Because
$g_p(n,n)=-1\neq0$, an observer is timelike and in particular nonzero
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). Observers at $p$ exist:
the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and
$n:=N_p/\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}$ satisfies $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and
$g_p(n,N_p)=-\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}<0$, where the square root is the
nonnegative root of [[def-rational-power]]; then $-n$ is a unit timelike
vector with $g_p(-n,N_p)>0$, so it is not an observer, and the two vectors
$n,-n$ point in opposite time directions.

**(b) Rest space.** For an observer $n$ at $p$, the **rest space** of $n$ is
the $g_p$-orthogonal complement of the line $\mathbb Rn$,

$$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM: g_p(v,n)=0\},$$

in the sense of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. It is
a linear subspace of $T_pM$. The further facts that $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and
that the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive definite are proved
in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]; they are consequences, not
part of the definition.

**(c) Spatial projection.** The **spatial projection** of the observer $n$ is
the map

$$h_n:T_pM\longrightarrow T_pM,\qquad h_n(v):=v+g_p(n,v)\,n .$$

The map is linear because $g_p$ is bilinear, its image is contained in
$n^{\perp}$, and it fixes $n^{\perp}$ pointwise; that it is the
$g_p$-orthogonal projection onto $n^{\perp}$ with kernel $\mathbb Rn$ is
proved in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]].

**(d) Scope.** An observer at $p$ is a single tangent vector. It is not an
ordered basis or frame of $T_pM$, not a chart, not a field of observers such as
the congruences defined later on this page, and not a curve or a worldline: no
parametrized curve, clock reading, proper time or measurement is attached to
$n$ by this definition. The physical reading of an observer as the direction
of an ideal clock's worldline, and the measurement interpretation of the
observer-relative quantities introduced later on this page, belong to the
physical postulates and unit conventions of the framework and are not asserted
here.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with associated quadratic form
$q(v)=\eta(v,v)$. A vector $v\in V$ is

- **timelike** when $q(v)<0$;
- **null**, or **lightlike**, when $v\neq 0$ and $q(v)=0$;
- **spacelike** when $q(v)>0$;
- **causal** when it is timelike or null.

The zero vector $0\in V$ satisfies $q(0)=0$ and is consequently **none** of
timelike, null or spacelike: the null case explicitly excludes it, and the
timelike and spacelike cases exclude it by $q(0)=0$ together with the strict
inequalities. The **causal character** of a nonzero vector $v$ is the sign of
the real number $q(v)$, and the three names are attached to the three signs as
above. When no confusion arises, the pairing $\eta$ itself is written
$\langle v,w\rangle:=\eta(v,w)$.

**Each nonzero vector has exactly one causal character.** For a nonzero
$v\in V$ the real number $q(v)$ satisfies exactly one of $q(v)<0$, $q(v)=0$,
$q(v)>0$ by trichotomy of the order on $\mathbb R$, so $v$ is timelike, null or
spacelike, and no two of the three alternatives can hold at once. The causal
vectors are therefore exactly the nonzero vectors that are timelike or null,
and the zero vector is causal in no sense introduced here.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary, so that $M$ is Hausdorff
and second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $g$ be a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Then $g$ assigns
to every $p\in M$ a bilinear form $g_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(a) Lorentzian metric.** The field $g$ is a **Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$** on $M$ when it is symmetric and nondegenerate, and at every
$p\in M$ the pair $(T_pM,g_p)$ is a Lorentz vector space of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]: that is, $g_p$ has
inertia $(3,1,0)$, so that some — equivalently every — basis of $T_pM$ in which
the matrix of $g_p$ is diagonal has exactly one negative and three positive
diagonal entries. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** (or
Lorentzian manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$). In a smooth chart $(U,x)$ the
**components** of $g$ are the $C^\infty$ functions
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and $g_{ab}=g_{ba}$ by symmetry.
We use indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ and the Einstein summation convention, with
components in a chart written as lower-case indexed symbols and equations
between indexed fields understood basis-independently. These conventions are
fixed once for this library and the physical reading of the symbols is recorded
with the framework postulates, separately from this mathematical definition.

**(b) Pointwise causal structure.** For every $p\in M$ the vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] applies to the Lorentz vector
space $(T_pM,g_p)$: a tangent vector $v\in T_pM$ is **timelike** when
$g_p(v,v)<0$, **null** when $v\neq0$ and $g_p(v,v)=0$, **spacelike** when
$g_p(v,v)>0$, and **causal** when it is timelike or null. Every nonzero
$v\in T_pM$ has exactly one causal character. The **timelike set**
$T_p:=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\}$ has exactly two connected components, each
nonempty, open, convex and path-connected; each $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $T_pM$ satisfies $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
for some ordering, so in particular nonzero orthonormal vectors exist at every
point ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]],
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

**(c) Time orientation.** A **time orientation** of $(M,g)$, also called a
**choice of future cone**, is a smooth vector field $N$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]], whose tangent-bundle
smooth structure uses the axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of
[[def-countable-choice]]; this is the only use of that axiom in this
definition) such that

$$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in M .$$

The function $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N_p)$ is $C^\infty$ because $g$ is a smooth
covariant $2$-tensor field and $N$ a smooth field, so the condition is a
pointwise strict inequality between a smooth function and $0$; since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0$ implies $N_p\neq0$, a time orientation is nowhere vanishing.
A **time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** is a triple $(M,g,N)$
consisting of a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and a time orientation $N$.

Given a time orientation $N$ and $p\in M$, the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and we
**define** a nonzero causal vector $v\in T_pM$ to be **future-directed** when
$g_p(v,N_p)<0$ and **past-directed** when $g_p(v,N_p)>0$. The classification of
nonzero causal vectors into exactly these two classes, and its agreement with
the two components of the timelike set (the future component is the component
$C_p^+$ containing $N_p$, and the future causal vectors form
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$), is proved in
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]; in particular no
nonzero causal $v$ satisfies $g_p(v,N_p)=0$, so the definition is exhaustive and
mutually exclusive. Replacing $N$ by $-N$ reverses every future/past label, and
two time orientations $N,N'$ determine the same future-directed causal vectors
at every point where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)<0$, while they determine opposite ones
where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)>0$, by
[[lem-gr-timelike-fields-define-equal-or-opposite-future-cones]]; that lemma
also shows the sign of $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N'_p)$ is constant on every connected
component of $M$.

**(d) The inverse metric.** Because $g_p$ is nondegenerate, it induces at each
$p$ an isomorphism $\flat_p:T_pM\to T_p^*M$, $v\mapsto g_p(v,\cdot)$, and an
inverse metric $g_p^{-1}$ on the dual space; the inverse metric, the musical
isomorphisms and the components $g^{ab}$ are defined separately on this page,
where the smoothness of those components is also proved. Neither construction
uses any choice principle beyond the one already recorded in (c).


**(e) Smooth timelike curves and their scalar normalization.** Before using
these quantities in the physical conventions, fix a positive real scaling
parameter $c$ (with no physical meaning or dimension in this mathematical
item). A **smooth future timelike curve** is a smooth map $\gamma:I\to M$
from a nonempty open real interval $I$ ([[def-interval]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) whose velocity derivation
$\gamma'(s)\in T_{\gamma(s)}M$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]]) satisfies
$g(\gamma',\gamma')<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)<0$ at every $s\in I$.
In a chart its components are $d(x^a\circ\gamma)/ds$, $a=0,1,2,3$.
For a supplied base point $s_0\in I$ and additive constant $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$
define

$$h(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s))},\qquad \tau(s):=\tau_0+\frac1c\int_{s_0}^{s}h(r)\,dr,\qquad U(s):=\frac{c\gamma'(s)}{h(s)}.$$

The integral is oriented when $s<s_0$. The function $\tau$ is called
**proper time** for this scaling and $U$ the **four-velocity** of the smooth
curve; its increment times $c$ is the Lorentzian length. The well-definedness
proof below shows $\tau'>0$, that $\tau:I\to\tau(I)$ is a smooth
diffeomorphism, and that $U$ is the velocity of $\gamma\circ\tau^{-1}$.
Thus $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and $U$ is future timelike. This introduces the smooth
case before any physical unit reading; the later worldline definition extends
it to its stated $C^k$, endpoint and piecewise-$C^1$ classes. It asserts no
clock coupling, motion law or physical value of $c$.

**Convention and scope.** The physical reading of a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold as a classical spacetime model, and the domain in which
that reading is adopted, are recorded in the framework postulate
`post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain`; the words spacetime and event carry no
mathematical content beyond this definition, and this item asserts no claim
about nature. The dimension $4$ and the absence of boundary are part of the
data; nothing in the definition assumes that $M$ is nonempty or connected, and
no completeness, extendibility or maximality property of $(M,g)$ is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
subset carrying the restricted smooth structure of
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]],
let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), and let $n$ be a smooth observer
congruence on $U$ ([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]), so that
$g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $n_p$ is future-directed at every $p\in U$.

**(a) Spatial projection field.** Let

$$h^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$$

on $U$, the component expression of the field of $g$-orthogonal projections
onto the rest spaces $n_p^{\perp}$ of [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]
([[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]); at every $p$ one has
$h^a{}_bn^b=0$, $n_a h^a{}_b=0$, $h^a{}_bh^b{}_c=h^a{}_c$ and
$h^a{}_a=3$. The field is smooth because $n$, $g$ and the identity are smooth
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]).

**(b) Measured energy density.** The **measured energy density** of $T$ for the
congruence $n$ is the smooth function

$$\mu:=T_{ab}n^an^b:U\to\mathbb R .$$

**(c) Energy-momentum current.** The **energy-momentum current** of $T$ for the
congruence $n$ is the smooth vector field on $U$ obtained by raising one index
of $T$ with the inverse metric and contracting with $n$,

$$J^a:=-T^{ab}n_b,$$

with $T^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}T_{cd}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]); the minus sign is the convention that
fixes the energy-component sign convention. A positive $\mu$
alone does not imply that $J$ is causal: $J$ may have an arbitrarily large
spatial part. No future-causal property of $J$ is imposed by this definition.

**(d) Energy flux.** The **energy flux** of $T$ for the congruence $n$ is the
smooth vector field

$$\Phi^a:=h^a{}_bJ^b=J^a-\mu n^a,$$

the spatial projection of $J$; it satisfies $n_a\Phi^a=0$ and
$\Phi^a=-h^a{}_bT^{bc}n_c$.

**(e) Spatial stress.** The **spatial stress** of $T$ for the congruence $n$ is
the smooth field obtained by projecting both tensor slots,

$$S^{ab}:=h^a{}_ch^b{}_dT^{cd},$$

which is symmetric in $a,b$ and satisfies $S^{ab}n_b=0$.

The identities $\mu=-J^an_a$, $J=\mu n+\Phi$, $S^{ab}n_b=0$ and the orthogonal
decomposition

$$T^{ab}=\mu n^an^b+n^a\Phi^b+n^b\Phi^a+S^{ab},$$

together with the uniqueness of that decomposition and the component formulas
in a $g$-orthonormal frame, are proved in
[[lem-gr-observer-energy-momentum-decomposition]]; this definition asserts
none of them. The physical reading and the units of $\mu$, $\Phi$ and $S$ are
fixed by the framework's reading on this page and are not asserted here.

Adopt the framework's unit and reading conventions
([[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]) and the stress-energy slot
([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented
smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset,
let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$ and let $n$ be
a smooth observer congruence on $U$
([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]). Let $\mu$, $J$, $\Phi$
and $S$ be the fields of [[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]].

**(a) Measured energy density and its unit.** The smooth function
$\mu=T_{ab}n^an^b$ is read as the **energy density measured by the observers of
the congruence $n$**, with numerical values in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ when
$T$ is read in the orthonormal-frame convention of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]] clauses (a) and (d). The same item fixes
the energy-density reading of $\rho_n=T(n,n)$ for a future unit timelike
$n$.

**(b) Energy flux and momentum density.** The smooth spatial vector field
$\Phi=h(J)$ of [[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]] is the tensor's
spatial current in the normalized observer convention. Its components have
energy-density units, $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$. Define the **SI measured
energy-flux vector** $q:=c\Phi$ and **SI measured momentum-density covector**
$p:=\Phi^{\flat}/c$, where $\Phi^{\flat}(a)=g(\Phi,a)$ and $c$ is the
conversion constant of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]].
In every ordered orthonormal basis with future $e_0=n_p$,

$$\Phi^i=T^{0i}=-T(e_0,e_i),\qquad q^i=c\Phi^i,\qquad p_i=\Phi^i/c,\qquad i=1,2,3,$$

by [[lem-gr-observer-energy-momentum-decomposition]] (d). Hence $q^i$ has
units $\mathrm W\,\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $p_i$ has units
$\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-2}\mathrm s^{-1}$; equivalently $q^{\flat}=c^2p$.
When the algebraic balance formulas call $\Phi$ an energy flux they use this
normalized tensor current, whose SI energy flux is $c\Phi$. The analogous
natural-unit momentum notation suppresses the factor $1/c$; it never assigns
SI momentum units directly to $\Phi^{\flat}$. Symmetry of $T$ gives the two
aspects of the same mixed component, with these distinct SI conversions.

**(c) Measured stress.** Write $S_{ab}=g_{ac}g_{bd}S^{cd}$ for the covariant
form of the projected field of [[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]]
clause (e). Explicitly, for $p\in U$ and $v,w\in T_pM$,
$S_p(v,w):=T_p(h_p(v),h_p(w))$, where
$h_p(v)=v+g_p(n_p,v)n_p$. This agrees with the lowered component formula
because $h_p$ is self-adjoint for $g_p$. This smooth symmetric covariant field
is read as the **stress measured by the observers** of the congruence: for unit spatial vectors
$e,e'$ in the rest space of $n_p$, $S_p(e,e')$ is read as the force per unit
area in the direction $e$ across a surface whose normal is $e'$, with
components in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ by the conventions.

**(d) Current and charge reading.** For this clause choose an orientation on
$U$ and the volume form of its restricted metric; this choice is independent
of the time orientation. The smooth vector field $J$ of
[[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]] clause (c) is read as the
**energy-momentum current density measured by the congruence**, and for a
finite smooth singular $3$-chain $\Sigma$ of $U$ the flux $\Phi_J(\Sigma)$ of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) is read as the
energy-momentum assigned to $\Sigma$ by the congruence, in the sense of the
charge reading of that item. For a $3$-chain carried by a spacelike slice
whose normal is (up to sign) $n$, the index-lowered component $-J_an^a=\mu$ is
the density integrated in that reading.

**(e) Scope.** The reading is interpretive and applies to every prescribed
smooth symmetric $T$ and every observer congruence. No positivity of $\mu$, no
conservation of $J$, no dynamics, no existence of a matter model realizing $T$
and no measurement is asserted; the definition is confined to the smooth
branch of the framework, and $T$ need not satisfy any field equation.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b,\qquad g_{ac}(q)g^{cb}(q)=\delta_a{}^b,$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

Let $M$ be a smooth $n$-manifold ([[def-smooth-manifold]]), with smooth atlas
$\mathcal A$ and maximal smooth atlas $[\mathcal A]$
([[def-smooth-atlas]], [[def-smoothly-compatible-charts]]). For $p\in M$ the
tangent space $T_pM$ is the real vector space of derivations at $p$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]), and the cotangent space is its
algebraic dual $T_p^*M:=(T_pM)^*$
([[def-cotangent-space-and-cotangent-bundle-as-a-disjoint-union]]).

A **covariant $2$-tensor at $p$** is a bilinear map
$A_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$. It is **symmetric** when
$A_p(v,w)=A_p(w,v)$ for all $v,w\in T_pM$, and **nondegenerate** when the only
$v\in T_pM$ with $A_p(v,w)=0$ for all $w\in T_pM$ is $v=0$.

A **smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$** is a family $A=(A_p)_{p\in M}$
assigning to each $p$ a covariant $2$-tensor $A_p$ at $p$, such that for every
chart $(U,x)$ of the maximal smooth atlas $[\mathcal A]$ the **component
functions**

$$A_{ab}(q):=A_q\!\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial x^a}\Big|_q,\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x^b}\Big|_q\right),\qquad q\in U,$$

are $C^\infty$ on $U$. Here $\partial/\partial x^a|_q$ is the coordinate
derivation at $q$ ([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]],
[[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), the index
ranges over the label set $I_n=\{1,\dots,n\}$ (or the relabelled set
$I_4=\{0,1,2,3\}$ when $n=4$), and smoothness of the real-valued functions
$A_{ab}$ on the open set $U\subseteq M$ is the notion of
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]] applied to $M$ and
$\mathbb R$.

For a coordinate tuple $z\in x(U)$ define the **coordinate representative**
$A^x_{ab}(z):=A_{ab}(x^{-1}(z))$. When the argument is a coordinate tuple,
$A_{ab}(z)$ abbreviates this representative in the named chart; when it is a
point of $M$, it denotes the component function on the chart domain. Thus
$A_{ab}(x(y^{-1}(u)))$ in a change-of-coordinates formula means
$A^x_{ab}((x\circ y^{-1})(u))$, never evaluation of a function on $M$ at a
tuple. For $n=4$, $x^a$ and $\partial_a$ mean the original coordinate and
derivation labelled $a+1$, respectively; this relabels every slot and sum.
The label $0$ alone gives no coordinate vector a causal character.

Because the coordinate derivations at $q$ form a basis of $T_qM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), specifying
$A$ is the same as specifying the matrix of component functions in each chart;
[[lem-gr-covariant-two-tensor-transformation-law]] proves that the smoothness
requirement is independent of the chart used, so that the condition may be
checked on any smooth atlas of $M$, and derives the transformation law relating
components in two overlapping charts.

The field is **symmetric** when $A_p$ is symmetric for every $p\in M$, which in
a chart is the identity $A_{ab}=A_{ba}$ of component functions; it is
**nondegenerate** when $A_p$ is nondegenerate for every $p$, which in a chart is
the nonvanishing at every point of the polynomial function
$\det(A_{ab})$ of the components. The **matrix** of $A$ in a chart means the
matrix $\bigl(A_{ab}(q)\bigr)$ of its component functions at $q$.

**Convention.** In the four-dimensional case $n=4$ used in this library, indices
are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ with $0$ the time-coordinate label when such a coordinate is chosen, and we write
$A_{ab}$ for the components. A covariant $2$-tensor field is also called a
**$(0,2)$ tensor field**.

derivations.claim: (Two congruences.) By [L1], $n$ and $n'$ are both smooth observer congruences on $U:=\mathbb R^4$, and they are distinct because $n'$ has the nonzero spatial component $\gamma\beta\partial_1$.

(The tensor.) $T^{ab}=\rho\,u^au^b$ is the tensor of the dust model $(\rho,\partial_0)$; it is a smooth symmetric type $(2,0)$ tensor field, equivalently $T_{ab}=\rho\,\partial_{0,a}\partial_{0,b}$ after lowering both indices with [L3].
(Energy density for the static congruence.) For $n=\partial_0$, [L3] gives $u_an^a=\partial_{0,a}\delta^a_0=-1$, so $\mu=T_{ab}n^an^b=\rho(u_an^a)^2=\rho$ by [L2].

(Energy density for the boosted congruence.) For $n'$, [L1] and [L3] give $u_an'^a=\gamma\partial_{0,a}\bigl(\delta^a_0+\beta\delta^a_1\bigr)=-\gamma$. Hence $\mu'=T_{ab}n'^an'^b=\rho(u_an'^a)^2=\rho\gamma^2$ by [L2], and $\mu'-\mu=\rho(\gamma^2-1)>0$ because $\beta\in(0,1)$ implies $\gamma>1$.

(Conclusion.) The fixed smooth symmetric tensor $T$ assigns the energy density $\rho$ to the congruence $n$ and $\rho\gamma^2$ to the congruence $n'$, and these values differ since $\gamma>1$. The displayed statement is therefore refuted: in the framework's reading, measured energy density is observer dependent. This completes the counterexample.

boundaries.reason: Both congruences live on all of $\mathbb R^4$ and the refuted statement quantifies over a nonempty open $U$; no empty-domain case is needed for the refutation.

boundaries.evidence: step 2.2: the two measured densities differ by $\rho(\gamma^2-1)>0$; this nonvanishing difference refutes the statement, and the value $\beta=0$, which would make it vanish, is excluded by $\beta\in(0,1)$.
step 1.1: the two congruences differ in the single parameter $\beta$, and that one number already produces $\mu'-\mu=\rho(\gamma^2-1)\neq0$.

boundaries.reason: Both congruences are unit timelike for $\beta\in(0,1)$; the null limit $\beta\to1$ is excluded and no degenerate congruence is treated.
The comparison is pointwise on $\mathbb R^4$ and involves no interval, curve or chain endpoint.
Both congruences and the tensor are displayed explicitly; the counterexample selects nothing, and $\gamma>0$ is the positive square root fixed by $\beta\in(0,1)$.

boundaries.evidence: step 3.1: the refuted implication is universally quantified over pairs of congruences; the exhibited pair $n,n'$ with $\mu\neq\mu'$ is exactly a failure of its conclusion under its hypothesis.

boundaries.reason: The refuted statement contains no reverse implication, and the counterexample does not claim that all observer congruences disagree.

risk_review.notes: Steps 1.1–3.1 checked: 0<beta<1 gives future unit n prime, gamma>1, T=rho u-flat tensor u-flat, and energies rho versus rho gamma^2. Endpoints beta=0 and beta=1 are explicitly excluded; rho>0 makes strict inequality. These are conditional model readings, not observations; no field-law assertion. Uses only density clause (a), unaffected by stress clarification.

citations.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

**(b) Torsion freedom.** The **torsion** of $\nabla$ is the tangent-valued
$2$-tensor $T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$ of
[[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]], with bracket as in
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. The connection is **torsion-free**
when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all smooth $X,Y$, that is, when
$\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$ identically.

**(c) Metric-selected connections.** A **metric-selected connection** for
$(M,g)$ is an affine connection on $M$ that is both torsion-free and
$g$-compatible. Equivalently, it is an element of the class

$$\operatorname{LC}(M,g):=\{\nabla:\nabla\text{ is an affine connection on }M,\ \nabla\text{ is torsion-free and }g\text{-compatible}\}.$$

The name records that the pair of conditions selects the connection out of all
affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.


**(d) Intrinsic construction before physical use.** For smooth local vector
fields define the Koszul expression

$$K(X,Y,Z):=Xg(Y,Z)+Yg(Z,X)-Zg(X,Y)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X).$$

Define $\nabla^g_XY$ by $2g(\nabla^g_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)$ for every smooth local
$Z$. The proof below establishes existence, smoothness, the affine-connection
rules, metric compatibility, torsion freedom and uniqueness; it uses symmetry
and nondegeneracy, not positive definiteness. Thus $\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$
has this unique element, called the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$. The later
nondegenerate-metric theorem retains its fuller tensor-derivative statement.
Its Christoffel symbols in any chart are defined by
$\nabla^g_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]) and obey

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12 g^{ad}(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}),\qquad a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3.$$

**(e) Basic curvature and contractions.** The **curvature** of this connection
is the operator of [[def-curvature-of-an-affine-connection]], with the fixed
sign convention

$$R^g(X,Y)Z:=\nabla^g_X\nabla^g_YZ-\nabla^g_Y\nabla^g_XZ-\nabla^g_{[X,Y]}Z.$$

The general affine-connection theorem
[[thm-curvature-is-a-type-one-three-tensor]] proves that it depends pointwise
only on $X,Y,Z$ and is a smooth tensor. Define its chart components by
$R^g(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=R^a{}_{bcd}\partial_a$.
Define the **Ricci tensor** and **scalar curvature** pointwise by

$$\operatorname{Ric}_p(v,w):=\operatorname{tr}(z\mapsto R^g_p(z,w)v),\qquad S(p):=\operatorname{tr}(\sharp_p\circ\operatorname{Ric}^{\flat}_p),\qquad \operatorname{Ric}^{\flat}_p(v):=\operatorname{Ric}_p(v,\cdot).$$

Here $\sharp$ is the inverse metric isomorphism and traces are the
basis-independent trace of [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. Equivalently,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=\sum_aR^a{}_{bad}$ and
$S=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}$, all sums from $0$ through $3$.
These are well-defined smooth fields by finite contraction of the smooth
components of $R^g$ and $g^{-1}$; basis independence follows from the trace
and the intrinsic maps just defined. No symmetry identity or field equation
is assumed here. Lowering the curvature output gives
$R_{abcd}=g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd}$, so the definitions agree with the full later
curvature item, which proves the remaining symmetries and coordinate formulas.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b,\qquad g_{ac}(q)g^{cb}(q)=\delta_a{}^b,$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

Let $M$ be a smooth $n$-manifold ([[def-smooth-manifold]]), with smooth atlas
$\mathcal A$ and maximal smooth atlas $[\mathcal A]$
([[def-smooth-atlas]], [[def-smoothly-compatible-charts]]). For $p\in M$ the
tangent space $T_pM$ is the real vector space of derivations at $p$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]), and the cotangent space is its
algebraic dual $T_p^*M:=(T_pM)^*$
([[def-cotangent-space-and-cotangent-bundle-as-a-disjoint-union]]).

A **covariant $2$-tensor at $p$** is a bilinear map
$A_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$. It is **symmetric** when
$A_p(v,w)=A_p(w,v)$ for all $v,w\in T_pM$, and **nondegenerate** when the only
$v\in T_pM$ with $A_p(v,w)=0$ for all $w\in T_pM$ is $v=0$.

A **smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$** is a family $A=(A_p)_{p\in M}$
assigning to each $p$ a covariant $2$-tensor $A_p$ at $p$, such that for every
chart $(U,x)$ of the maximal smooth atlas $[\mathcal A]$ the **component
functions**

$$A_{ab}(q):=A_q\!\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial x^a}\Big|_q,\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x^b}\Big|_q\right),\qquad q\in U,$$

are $C^\infty$ on $U$. Here $\partial/\partial x^a|_q$ is the coordinate
derivation at $q$ ([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]],
[[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), the index
ranges over the label set $I_n=\{1,\dots,n\}$ (or the relabelled set
$I_4=\{0,1,2,3\}$ when $n=4$), and smoothness of the real-valued functions
$A_{ab}$ on the open set $U\subseteq M$ is the notion of
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]] applied to $M$ and
$\mathbb R$.

For a coordinate tuple $z\in x(U)$ define the **coordinate representative**
$A^x_{ab}(z):=A_{ab}(x^{-1}(z))$. When the argument is a coordinate tuple,
$A_{ab}(z)$ abbreviates this representative in the named chart; when it is a
point of $M$, it denotes the component function on the chart domain. Thus
$A_{ab}(x(y^{-1}(u)))$ in a change-of-coordinates formula means
$A^x_{ab}((x\circ y^{-1})(u))$, never evaluation of a function on $M$ at a
tuple. For $n=4$, $x^a$ and $\partial_a$ mean the original coordinate and
derivation labelled $a+1$, respectively; this relabels every slot and sum.
The label $0$ alone gives no coordinate vector a causal character.

Because the coordinate derivations at $q$ form a basis of $T_qM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), specifying
$A$ is the same as specifying the matrix of component functions in each chart;
[[lem-gr-covariant-two-tensor-transformation-law]] proves that the smoothness
requirement is independent of the chart used, so that the condition may be
checked on any smooth atlas of $M$, and derives the transformation law relating
components in two overlapping charts.

The field is **symmetric** when $A_p$ is symmetric for every $p\in M$, which in
a chart is the identity $A_{ab}=A_{ba}$ of component functions; it is
**nondegenerate** when $A_p$ is nondegenerate for every $p$, which in a chart is
the nonvanishing at every point of the polynomial function
$\det(A_{ab})$ of the components. The **matrix** of $A$ in a chart means the
matrix $\bigl(A_{ab}(q)\bigr)$ of its component functions at $q$.

**Convention.** In the four-dimensional case $n=4$ used in this library, indices
are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ with $0$ the time-coordinate label when such a coordinate is chosen, and we write
$A_{ab}$ for the components. A covariant $2$-tensor field is also called a
**$(0,2)$ tensor field**.

Let $(M,\mathcal S)$ be a smooth $n$-manifold and let $U\subseteq M$ be open,
carrying the subspace topology. Then $U$ is a topological $n$-manifold. For
every smooth atlas $\mathcal A$ with $[\mathcal A]=\mathcal S$, the family of
restricted charts

$$\mathcal A|_U:=\bigl\{\,\bigl(V\cap U,\ \varphi|_{V\cap U}\bigr):(V,\varphi)\in\mathcal A\,\bigr\}.$$

is a smooth atlas on $U$, and the maximal atlas it generates is independent of
the presenting atlas $\mathcal A$: it depends only on the structure
$\mathcal S$. This maximal atlas is the **restricted smooth structure** of $U$.

Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth manifolds, let $F:M\to N$ be a map, let $p\in M$ and
let $r\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$, where $\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$.
For $m,q\in\mathbb N_0$ and an open set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, a map
$g:E\to\mathbb R^q$ is **of class $C^r$** as follows. When $m=0$, every such
map is declared $C^r$. When $m\ge1$, each component $g_l$ with $l<q$ must be
$C^r$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]; when $q=0$ this
component condition is vacuous.
Suppose $F$ is continuous at $p$. Then $F$ is **of class $C^r$ at $p$** when
there are smooth charts $(U,\varphi)$ of $M$ at $p$ and $(V,\psi)$ of $N$ at
$F(p)$ with $F(U)\subseteq V$ such that the coordinate representative

$$\psi\circ F\circ\varphi^{-1}:\varphi(U)\longrightarrow\psi(V)$$

([[def-coordinate-representation-of-a-map]]) is of class $C^r$ on a
neighbourhood of $\varphi(p)$ in this componentwise Euclidean sense. By
[[lem-chart-independence-of-c-r-smoothness]], this condition is independent of
the chosen charts: if one such representative is $C^r$, then every one is, so
"some charts" may be read as "any charts". A map is **$C^r$ on an open set**
$W\subseteq M$ when it is continuous on $W$ and $C^r$ at every point of $W$. A
map that is $C^r$ for every finite $r$ — equivalently $C^\infty$ — is called
**smooth**; the term **$C^r$ map between smooth manifolds** is reserved for the
case where $F$ is continuous and the representative condition holds at every
point of $M$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
subset carrying the restricted smooth structure of
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]],
let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), and let $n$ be a smooth observer
congruence on $U$ ([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]), so that
$g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $n_p$ is future-directed at every $p\in U$.

**(a) Spatial projection field.** Let

$$h^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$$

on $U$, the component expression of the field of $g$-orthogonal projections
onto the rest spaces $n_p^{\perp}$ of [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]
([[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]); at every $p$ one has
$h^a{}_bn^b=0$, $n_a h^a{}_b=0$, $h^a{}_bh^b{}_c=h^a{}_c$ and
$h^a{}_a=3$. The field is smooth because $n$, $g$ and the identity are smooth
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]).

**(b) Measured energy density.** The **measured energy density** of $T$ for the
congruence $n$ is the smooth function

$$\mu:=T_{ab}n^an^b:U\to\mathbb R .$$

**(c) Energy-momentum current.** The **energy-momentum current** of $T$ for the
congruence $n$ is the smooth vector field on $U$ obtained by raising one index
of $T$ with the inverse metric and contracting with $n$,

$$J^a:=-T^{ab}n_b,$$

with $T^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}T_{cd}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]); the minus sign is the convention that
fixes the energy-component sign convention. A positive $\mu$
alone does not imply that $J$ is causal: $J$ may have an arbitrarily large
spatial part. No future-causal property of $J$ is imposed by this definition.

**(d) Energy flux.** The **energy flux** of $T$ for the congruence $n$ is the
smooth vector field

$$\Phi^a:=h^a{}_bJ^b=J^a-\mu n^a,$$

the spatial projection of $J$; it satisfies $n_a\Phi^a=0$ and
$\Phi^a=-h^a{}_bT^{bc}n_c$.

**(e) Spatial stress.** The **spatial stress** of $T$ for the congruence $n$ is
the smooth field obtained by projecting both tensor slots,

$$S^{ab}:=h^a{}_ch^b{}_dT^{cd},$$

which is symmetric in $a,b$ and satisfies $S^{ab}n_b=0$.

The identities $\mu=-J^an_a$, $J=\mu n+\Phi$, $S^{ab}n_b=0$ and the orthogonal
decomposition

$$T^{ab}=\mu n^an^b+n^a\Phi^b+n^b\Phi^a+S^{ab},$$

together with the uniqueness of that decomposition and the component formulas
in a $g$-orthonormal frame, are proved in
[[lem-gr-observer-energy-momentum-decomposition]]; this definition asserts
none of them. The physical reading and the units of $\mu$, $\Phi$ and $S$ are
fixed by the framework's reading on this page and are not asserted here.

Adopt the framework's unit and reading conventions
([[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]) and the stress-energy slot
([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented
smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset,
let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$ and let $n$ be
a smooth observer congruence on $U$
([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]). Let $\mu$, $J$, $\Phi$
and $S$ be the fields of [[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]].

**(a) Measured energy density and its unit.** The smooth function
$\mu=T_{ab}n^an^b$ is read as the **energy density measured by the observers of
the congruence $n$**, with numerical values in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ when
$T$ is read in the orthonormal-frame convention of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]] clauses (a) and (d). The same item fixes
the energy-density reading of $\rho_n=T(n,n)$ for a future unit timelike
$n$.

**(b) Energy flux and momentum density.** The smooth spatial vector field
$\Phi=h(J)$ of [[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]] is the tensor's
spatial current in the normalized observer convention. Its components have
energy-density units, $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$. Define the **SI measured
energy-flux vector** $q:=c\Phi$ and **SI measured momentum-density covector**
$p:=\Phi^{\flat}/c$, where $\Phi^{\flat}(a)=g(\Phi,a)$ and $c$ is the
conversion constant of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]].
In every ordered orthonormal basis with future $e_0=n_p$,

$$\Phi^i=T^{0i}=-T(e_0,e_i),\qquad q^i=c\Phi^i,\qquad p_i=\Phi^i/c,\qquad i=1,2,3,$$

by [[lem-gr-observer-energy-momentum-decomposition]] (d). Hence $q^i$ has
units $\mathrm W\,\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $p_i$ has units
$\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-2}\mathrm s^{-1}$; equivalently $q^{\flat}=c^2p$.
When the algebraic balance formulas call $\Phi$ an energy flux they use this
normalized tensor current, whose SI energy flux is $c\Phi$. The analogous
natural-unit momentum notation suppresses the factor $1/c$; it never assigns
SI momentum units directly to $\Phi^{\flat}$. Symmetry of $T$ gives the two
aspects of the same mixed component, with these distinct SI conversions.

**(c) Measured stress.** Write $S_{ab}=g_{ac}g_{bd}S^{cd}$ for the covariant
form of the projected field of [[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]]
clause (e). Explicitly, for $p\in U$ and $v,w\in T_pM$,
$S_p(v,w):=T_p(h_p(v),h_p(w))$, where
$h_p(v)=v+g_p(n_p,v)n_p$. This agrees with the lowered component formula
because $h_p$ is self-adjoint for $g_p$. This smooth symmetric covariant field
is read as the **stress measured by the observers** of the congruence: for unit spatial vectors
$e,e'$ in the rest space of $n_p$, $S_p(e,e')$ is read as the force per unit
area in the direction $e$ across a surface whose normal is $e'$, with
components in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ by the conventions.

**(d) Current and charge reading.** For this clause choose an orientation on
$U$ and the volume form of its restricted metric; this choice is independent
of the time orientation. The smooth vector field $J$ of
[[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]] clause (c) is read as the
**energy-momentum current density measured by the congruence**, and for a
finite smooth singular $3$-chain $\Sigma$ of $U$ the flux $\Phi_J(\Sigma)$ of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) is read as the
energy-momentum assigned to $\Sigma$ by the congruence, in the sense of the
charge reading of that item. For a $3$-chain carried by a spacelike slice
whose normal is (up to sign) $n$, the index-lowered component $-J_an^a=\mu$ is
the density integrated in that reading.

**(e) Scope.** The reading is interpretive and applies to every prescribed
smooth symmetric $T$ and every observer congruence. No positivity of $\mu$, no
conservation of $J$, no dynamics, no existence of a matter model realizing $T$
and no measurement is asserted; the definition is confined to the smooth
branch of the framework, and $T$ need not satisfy any field equation.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty
open subset, carrying the restricted smooth structure of
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]].

**(a) Congruences.** An **observer congruence** on $U$ is a smooth vector field
$n$ on $U$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]) such that
$n_q$ is an observer at $q$ for every $q\in U$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]); explicitly,

$$g_q(n_q,n_q)=-1\quad\text{and}\quad g_q(n_q,N_q)<0\qquad\text{for every }q\in U .$$

Since $g_q(n_q,n_q)=-1$, the field $n$ is nowhere vanishing. A single observer
at a point is therefore not a congruence, and a congruence is not an ordered
basis or frame of $T_qM$.

**(b) Observer curves.** Because $n$ is a smooth vector field on $U$, the
theorem on maximal integral curves
([[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]],
[[def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field]]) assigns to every $q\in U$ a unique
maximal integral curve $\gamma_q:I_q\to U$ of $n$ with $\gamma_q(0)=q$,
defined on an open interval $I_q\subseteq\mathbb R$. We call these curves the
**observers** (or **observer curves**) of the congruence. Each curve is regular:
for every $s\in I_q$, $\gamma_q'(s)=n_{\gamma_q(s)}$ and

$$g_{\gamma_q(s)}\bigl(n_{\gamma_q(s)},n_{\gamma_q(s)}\bigr)=-1,$$

so its tangent is nonzero, unit timelike and future-directed. Completeness of
the maximal intervals $I_q$, and global product or foliation structure of
$U$, are not asserted. The parameter $s$ is the flow parameter of $n$; it is
not identified with any clock reading here.

**(c) Adapted charts.** An **$n$-adapted chart** is a smooth chart
$(u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3):U'\to\mathbb R^4$ of $M$ whose domain $U'$ is a nonempty
open subset of $U$ and whose **spatial coordinates** $u^1,u^2,u^3$ are constant
along every integral curve $\gamma:J\to U'$ of the restricted field
$n|_{U'}$, where $J$ is an interval. Equivalently, for each maximal observer
curve $\gamma_q:I_q\to U$, each connected component $K$ of
$\gamma_q^{-1}(U')$ (a maximal nonempty interval contained in this open
subset of $\mathbb R$), and $i=1,2,3$, the function
$u^i\circ\gamma_q$ is constant on $K$. If $q\in U'$ and $0\in K$, this
constant is $u^i(q)$. This condition does not identify labels on different
components when a maximal curve leaves and re-enters $U'$. No global adapted
chart, and no adapted chart on all of $U$, is
asserted by this definition; one exists near every point of $U$ by the
existence corollary proved on this page.

**(d) Scope.** A congruence is a field of observer directions on an open set; it
is not a chart, not a tetrad field, and not a family of parametrized
worldlines with specified domains. The physical reading of its observer curves
as ideal-clock worldlines, and the identification of the flow parameter with a
measurable time, belong to the physical postulates of the framework and are not
asserted here.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with associated quadratic form
$q(v)=\eta(v,v)$. A vector $v\in V$ is

- **timelike** when $q(v)<0$;
- **null**, or **lightlike**, when $v\neq 0$ and $q(v)=0$;
- **spacelike** when $q(v)>0$;
- **causal** when it is timelike or null.

The zero vector $0\in V$ satisfies $q(0)=0$ and is consequently **none** of
timelike, null or spacelike: the null case explicitly excludes it, and the
timelike and spacelike cases exclude it by $q(0)=0$ together with the strict
inequalities. The **causal character** of a nonzero vector $v$ is the sign of
the real number $q(v)$, and the three names are attached to the three signs as
above. When no confusion arises, the pairing $\eta$ itself is written
$\langle v,w\rangle:=\eta(v,w)$.

**Each nonzero vector has exactly one causal character.** For a nonzero
$v\in V$ the real number $q(v)$ satisfies exactly one of $q(v)<0$, $q(v)=0$,
$q(v)>0$ by trichotomy of the order on $\mathbb R$, so $v$ is timelike, null or
spacelike, and no two of the three alternatives can hold at once. The causal
vectors are therefore exactly the nonzero vectors that are timelike or null,
and the zero vector is causal in no sense introduced here.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary, so that $M$ is Hausdorff
and second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $g$ be a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Then $g$ assigns
to every $p\in M$ a bilinear form $g_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(a) Lorentzian metric.** The field $g$ is a **Lorentzian metric of signature
